findings.input: A serving or training observation published by servingattempt.Record or trainingworkflow.Observer.finish when (a) the recipe-state read fails and the incoming Verification is empty, or (b) the same recipe is activated again, verified, after the recorded attempt executed it not verified.
findings.expected: Publication carries the state the executed recipe and task had at execution. A failed state read is told apart from a historical absent state and earns no verified credit, and a later activation does not replace execution-time state. Legacy bytes, the own-verifying-run exception and partial or cancelled results keep their contract.
findings.actual: The two remaining owners still read state at publication and drop the lookup error: servingattempt.Record (servingattempt.go:117-119) and Observer.finish (session_observation.go:271-273). A failed read leaves an empty Verification; scorecard.unverifiedAside rejects only explicit not-verified/broken and accepts that empty value as legacy. A later same-recipe activation is written as the attempt's state in place of its execution-time not-verified state. Shown from source at 8acbf71d17dfd3e1e35313b370f900b21f0fdf10; no SQA execution.

findings.input: (3) Gemma accuracy over 32 independent media, each with two uniformly guessed 3-choice questions. (4) Two judges ranked on all-constant finite scores, and on probabilities (.9,.1) against (.45,.45). (6) Two GIF media inputs for their own bound renders, with one judge and scorer, decoded at 16 frames against 1. (7) The embedded SenseNova APG verdict edited to 0 wins, 524 losses, 0 ties, 80 media and tail 0.0001, Admitted left true, with Says changed consistently to 'admitted: a gain beyond chance, 0 wins, 524 losses and 0 ties over 80 media'; its evaluation IDs stay unchanged. (8) A render campaign resumed after an earlier item's request changed while its last item drew the same, or with truncated bookkeeping.
findings.expected: (3) The accuracy null matches the actual choice counts and within-media dependence. (4) Ranking uses the aggregation production scores with, and an undefined tau or omitted resamples are said, without a panic. (6) A reading is admitted only from evaluations bound to the same render, decode sampling and question contract, and a control offers a candidate only by the admission for its own model, recipe and request. (7) The record's verdict, counts and tail are derived through AdmitPreset and its bound evaluations, so drift is refused. (8) A completed arm or verdict is reused only for the same bound inputs, evaluator and producer; changed work is refused or redone, and truncated bookkeeping does not count as complete.
findings.actual: (3) Correct count minus sum(1/choices) against zero is taken as a fair sign for ExactPairedBinary: a medium is positive with probability 5/9, and uniform guessing passes the 22-positive threshold (nominal tail 0.0250512) with probability 0.0914273, above the 0.05 level. (4) Arithmetic probability means rank (.9,.1) above (.45,.45), the reverse of production softShare's geometric mean; constant scores give a NaN tau, all 2000 resamples are dropped and resampledTau indexes an empty slice. (6) judgedRender compares content, request, producer, runtime and scorer but not MediaInput.Decode or the question contract, readRender never calls verifyRendered, ResolveActiveExecution takes the current activation, and the embedded offering uses recorded no-loss flags (plus a recorded gain for guidance methods) under a published model name/preset key, without runtime recipe/request binding. (7) The native record test checks evaluation-ID syntax, displayed counts and admitted/refused wording, but does not recompute Admitted or Tail through AdmitPreset and the bound evaluations. Gained trusts Tail <= falseGain, so the consistently worded false gain in input 7 passes the record and gain checks and offers APG on SenseNova's page despite its stated 524 losses and zero wins. (8) Arm, suite and verdict skips trust names and file existence and accept truncated bookkeeping, and a new build is validated by re-rendering only the last item. Remaining counterexamples shown from source and arithmetic at 0c24aca5b670940f95c0f8156c13804a9e2fd9ea; no SQA execution.

findings.input: A retained ClipMotion observation of unchanged MP4 bytes, then a motion encoder checkpoint or FFmpeg/preprocessing configuration changes under the same encoder basename. The suite is compiled again with that old observation and the same matching clip-content digest.
findings.expected: Motion readings identify the encoder/checkpoint and decoder/sampling contract that produced them, so changed instruments cannot silently reuse or be credited with an old metric. Keep the repaired OCR re-keying, content checks and whole-set exclusion in the existing media compiler and observation producers; the observation instrument is separate from the answering judge.
findings.actual: The remaining motion instrument is not bound: writeMotion passes filepath.Base(encoderPath) to measureMotion; ClipMotion stores that Encoder string and clip/source content digests, with no encoder/checkpoint or FFmpeg/sampling identity. ClipMotion.validate requires only a nonempty encoder name, and bindObservations compares clip.Content alone before keeping the motion set. Changing an instrument while the clip bytes and encoder basename stay the same therefore leaves the old motion admissible and its actual producing instrument indistinguishable. Shown from source at ba0405e63d92653b84f617d8c332d5546529e444; no SQA execution.

findings.input: A worker attempt interrupted between RunWorker recording its start and keepRunning writing the marker, or between removing the marker and the deferred end write; and a record from before 6da610a60, whose marker and attempt took separate time.Now values.
findings.expected: The interrupted attempt is reported with bounded known effort or an explicit unknown duration, downtime never counted as worker wall, and start, exit, restart and landing accounting share one lifecycle identity.
findings.actual: The start stays without a marker, noteUncleanEnd cannot close it, and landing.cost charges the elapsed time to now through the downtime; an old record cannot be matched by Step and Started. Two active-start stores remain. Worker-Wall-Seconds drops the unknown interrupted wall and printCosts presents the rest as worker wall with no qualification. Read from source.

findings.input: A tool call whose parameter value is exactly <, << or </param, followed by its closing </parameter>.
findings.expected: The grammar admits the value and the parser returns it unchanged; a complete closing tag still ends the value.
findings.actual: parameterLessThan makes every < consume a following character that diverges from </parameter>, so a value ending in a proper prefix of the tag consumes the real closing tag as another less-than rule and fails at its final >. The fixture's comment promises << but its map holds only longer text. Read from source.

findings.input: On a case-insensitive Windows checkout, a task with Files [scripts] and Tests [scripts/held_test.go] whose worker calls edit_file or delete_file on scripts/HELD_test.go.
findings.expected: Both tools refuse the other spelling of the held file before mutating it, its bytes and presence kept.
findings.actual: The held-test wrapper compares cleaned path strings with slices.Contains, so scripts/HELD_test.go misses the held name, stays under the allowed scripts directory and is admitted; os.WriteFile or os.Remove then rewrites or deletes the held test. Read from source.

findings.input: (1) After ComfyUI at revision A completes, /view fails. Retry the same accepted prompt after changing the installation to B. (2) Return two outputs of one node with the same basename in different subfolders. (3) Resume completed history or compare the retained 2368x1344 MOSS own-size run with overgo.
findings.expected: Preserve the accepted prompt's producer and both outputs. Identify the memory instrument and observation window, including missing samples on resume. Separate sampling setup from guided steps when comparing with ComfyUI progress intervals.
findings.actual: The receipt binds only prompt and request, so retry credits A's output to B. keep overwrites the same node/basename across subfolders. await samples whole-device Total-Free starting at retry. ownSizeReading compares 13.6 GiB of process allocations with 23.4 GiB of whole-device use, and 359 s after LoadGenerator with 58.123 s between reference execution events with cached nodes. At 39d27cd16 it still divides the entire integrate duration by steps. The retained 6fdcde850 profile measured 33.4 s of fixed sampling setup and 5.30 s per guided step. The reference's 1.11 s uses intervals between progress events and excludes initial setup.

findings.input: (1) A root package embedding value.txt, checked by go test . -run TestValue, with only value.txt changed. (2) A production file built with -tags=fixturelane embedding value.txt, checked by go test -tags=fixturelane ./p, with only value.txt changed.
findings.expected: The embedded asset enters the undo run's restoration set, so the unchanged test runs against the restored input and fails on its assertion.
findings.actual: (1) path.Dir(value.txt) is "." and the ancestor loop stops before adding it, so the asset is not restored and undoable says no production Go changed. (2) Production calls go list without the verifier's flags, so the tag-gated embed is not listed and the asset-only change skips the undo. Read from source.

findings.input: On a cache miss submit a fixed-seed MOSS request with a named, missing adapter. Install valid adapter weights after Contents checks the path but before modelAdapter opens it. After the request completes, remove the adapter and repeat. The same sequence applies to a required depth estimator for control.picture.
findings.expected: Reject missing required picture weights before lookup or model loading. Only a run bound to the content actually read may be reused. Keep the existing content-based replay and Windows read holds for present files, and allow requests that supply a depth map without an estimator.
findings.actual: Source at 5e82b8710. Contents hashes the literal 'absent' and continues on ErrNotExist without holding a file. The executor can then open the newly installed weights and publish their output under that absence key. When the file is missing again, the director returns the stored image before reopening it. Same-size replacements of files present at binding are fixed.

findings.input: Compare a recorded 1024x576 PNG to the same pixels with one extra column (1025x576). Separately, give the mirrored-input latent comparison a short vector or a NaN element while the unchanged baseline passes.
findings.expected: Check exact PNG dimensions in pictureDecibels and require nonempty, equal-length, finite latents in decibelsOverSquares before scoring. All three callers should use the same below-floor check for changed inputs. Exercise the malformed cases with small in-memory inputs. Preserve the recorded floors and +Inf for an exact match with nonzero signal.
findings.actual: Source at c79cfc121. squareColourMeans drops partial 8x8 tiles, so a 1025th column can leave the means identical. decibelsOverSquares returns -Inf for a length mismatch and propagates NaN. The golden-section, image-to-image and depth checks each reject only score >= floor, giving both invalid results credit as negative controls.

findings.input: Save a named prompt state on slot 0 with one supported model and max_concurrent=1. Make a rehearsal clone into a different directory. Serve the same model and recipe on that clone and POST /slots/0?action=restore with the saved filename and an idle slot.
findings.expected: Restore the saved state from the rehearsal's published object while preserving the source store, its alias, and its locations. Clone the immutable data without redundant full copies where the storage owner guarantees sharing is safe.
findings.actual: CloneStore links blobs/ but byte-copies objects/ and the database records with the original absolute locations. restoreSlot resolves the copied alias. objectstore.Open requires a published location equal to the clone's own object path, so it returns 'object store: object location is not published' and the route returns HTTP 500 despite the copied bytes. The clone fixture covers blob sharing and source survival; the slot fixture restores in its original directory. Source at 12f172302, no SQA execution.

findings.input: Complete a fixed-seed Wan prompt-to-video request with a writable store. Stop the server, install a different compatible umT5 checkpoint at the same path with the same byte count and modification time, then restart against the same store. Repeat the request with the same tokenizer, recipe and denoiser.
findings.expected: Verify that the current checkpoint matches the persisted identity before reusing the clip. The text-pipeline admission should reuse a proven unchanged checkpoint across restarts and compute again when its bytes change.
findings.actual: Source at 5e82b8710. TextPipelineIdentity loads the store memo. admitCheckpoint accepts its old digest on size and time alone. TestTextPipelineNamesItsCheckpointThroughTheStore explicitly expects the old name after a same-stat replacement even though a fresh digest differs. Reading passes that name to measuredRun, so the previous clip can replay before the new encoder runs. The replay consequence was traced from source.

findings.input: Use recipe run with an active LiveEdit model, a valid prompt and a stored source_artifact clip. In the otherwise valid clip-form JSON, give seed twice, first 7 then 8. An unknown field on the same form is also accepted.
findings.expected: Strictly decode each request once at resolveEditForm. Reject duplicate and unknown fields before clip resolution. Send both forms through the director's typed ExecuteInput path, preserving validation, authority checks and existing replay identities. TestClipFormRunRetainsItsRequest can check both forms and the refusals with its existing fixture.
findings.actual: Source at c79cfc121. resolveEditForm uses json.Unmarshal. A clip with duplicate seeds resolves and is recorded as an ordinary seed-8 request. A full request instead goes to next as raw text, so decodeJSONInput decodes its pixel and conditioning arrays again. The two-callback fixture requires that text handoff. Preserve the compact clip record and InputContent's digest for oversized full requests when removing it.

findings.input: After a passing needle-reference run, delete only fixtures/needle_upstream_calls.json and select lanes with -reached. The reader still names the old path. The same case applies to the models lane when only fixtures/moss/checkpoint.json is deleted.
findings.expected: CycleLanesReached selects the reader of the removed fixture, so the Needle or MOSS check reports the missing input. Use the existing reader lookup for deleted paths, or run the lane when its readers are unknown. Keep the current package selection for edits to existing fixtures.
findings.actual: Source trace at c71a1e230. The Git diff supplies the deleted path. TrackedDocuments lists only files still present, so documentReaders returns no entry. discover treats the missing entry as zero readers and omits the lane. Both checks fail on the missing file if selected. The retained gate verified selection for edits to both fixtures while they were present.

findings.input: In the existing mutantFixture, select a Go test that skips when Above(11) is false and otherwise passes. Above(v) returns v > 10. The baseline passes and reversing > to <= makes the only selected test skip.
findings.expected: Use the existing planverify verdict for Go tests. Count a failed test assertion as caught, a passing check as survived, and a skipped test or failed build as inconclusive. Exclude inconclusive attempts from the measured catch rate. The existing strong and weak fixture cases retain their verdicts.
findings.actual: Source trace at c79cfc121. planverify.Execute returns ErrVacuous for the skipped test. mutate counts every non-nil verifier error as Refused, so this example reports one of one caught without a failed assertion. A build failure before tests start earns the same credit. The undo checker already distinguishes ErrAssertion. The retained mutation totals do not identify why a mutation was counted as refused.

findings.input: On a cache miss, serve a 1024x576 MOSS request with prompt 'a fox', preset ultra-depth-control, a valid PNG in control.map and no control.end. Use the preset's installed adapters. The turbo depth preset has the same default.
findings.expected: Use the same resolved depth control when configuring and preparing the generator. An omitted end and an explicit 0.5 should both reach sampling with the recorded window. An explicit 1 must retain its own window, and a genuinely different request must still be rejected.
findings.actual: Source trace at 5dafd6d23. LoadGenerator or Reset applies withPreset, and prepare applies it again. Each call to withSection copies DepthControl to supply the default end. prepareRotary compares the two Request structs by pointer for Control and returns 'rotary image: request differs from loaded session' before sampling. The preset check asserts the filled value once. The depth image comparison supplies End explicitly and bypasses the failing branch.

findings.input: Give gguf.Write a 256-by-4 weight with dtype.I8ConvRot and its 1,040-byte payload, then open the output with gguf inspect.
findings.expected: Keep the GGUF file types explicit at the reader and writer boundary. Refuse type 44 before writing the header or accepting the tensor. The CUDA product can use I8ConvRot directly. Preserve the existing Gemma converter's explicit FP8 extension and its round trip.
findings.actual: Source trace at b11230b4b. NewTensorInfo and the reader both ask the runtime type for StorageBytes. Adding I8ConvRot to that table makes Write emit 44 and inspect report i8_convrot. The previous master refused 44. The local llama.cpp reader at 42fc24306 rejects it because GGML_TYPE_COUNT is 43.

findings.input: In the retained 256x3072 product, take the GPU result presented to the comparison and change a single positive zero in row 32 (zero-based) to the F32 value with bits 0x00000001. Leave every other result and the launch trace intact.
findings.expected: For moss-int8/do, have the existing product comparison reject a finite F32 result whose low 16 bits are nonzero before comparing its BF16 bits with the capture. The epilogue promises exact BF16 values in the F32 buffer consumed by the next graph node.
findings.actual: Source counterexample at b11230b4b. Row 32's retained digest matches 256 positive BF16 zeros. bf16Digest rounds each returned F32 to BF16, so the changed value also hashes as zero and both the row and whole-product comparisons pass. The committed epilogue does round its output. The check would also accept finite products with that last rounding removed.
